title: Lane Kiffin’s return to Ole Miss will have increased security — including 19 officers on horseback
content:
The most anticipated regular-season college football game of 2026 will have an increased security presence.

Saturday night, Lane Kiffin returns to Oxford, Miss., to lead his new team, No. 7 LSU, against the team he left for the Tigers, No. 8 Ole Miss. Kiffin took the LSU job last November in the middle of Ole Miss’ College Football Playoff run, sparking outrage among the Rebel fan base.

While the Oxford Police Department plans to treat the Tigers’ visit like any other Saturday in Oxford, the reality is it won’t be.

“It’s always all-hands on deck,” Oxford public information officer Breck Jones said.

Oxford PD has a staff of over 140 officers, all of whom will be deployed through Friday and Saturday in various shifts, Jones said. In addition, mounted patrol units from Mobile, Ala. and New Orleans will help patrol The Square, the cultural hub of downtown Oxford.

In total, 19 officers will be on horseback, with 13 from the Mobile and New Orleans units working alongside the six mounted officers who work for Oxford.

“The safety of our campus community and visitors is always a priority,” Daniel Sanford, director of Ole Miss University Police and Campus Safety, said in a statement. “While we cannot share specific security measures for safety reasons, University Police are working closely with local and state law enforcement partners to provide a safe and secure game-day environment.”

Sanford went on to say that the school has prepared for the larger expected crowd this weekend, and for fans to expect not only a greater law enforcement presence, but also expect some delays.

“We encourage everyone to allow plenty of time to navigate campus and to follow directions from law enforcement and game-day personnel,” Sanford said.

Kiffin’s departures from previous jobs have sparked intense levels of outrage. When he left Tennessee after one year as head coach of the Volunteers in 2009 to take the job at USC, students lit mattresses on fire on campus in Knoxville and posted videos of themselves urinating on T-shirts with Kiffin’s face on them.

Jones said that while Kiffin’s exit from Ole Miss was controversial, Oxford police did not field any disorderly conduct calls when Kiffin took the LSU job. A contingent of Ole Miss fans went to the Oxford airport when Kiffin departed and brandished their middle fingers when he boarded his private jet for Baton Rouge on Nov. 30, 2025.

Jones’ plea to anyone in town this weekend is to act responsibly and not let emotions get the best of them.

“It doesn’t matter who you are, what team you’re a fan of, we want to make sure everyone has a good time and gets home safely,” he said. “Don’t go beyond what you would normally do any other day. Have fun, but he responsible.”
